risk_assessment.rationale: The email requests an urgent change of payment details for an existing invoice from a lookalike domain not on file for the vendor, matching classic bank-detail-change fraud patterns.

signals.explanation: Sender domain is not on file and misspells the vendor name as 'stationary', closely resembling Fennimore Stationery Ltd.
Requests redirection of payment for invoice FS-2026-1182 to a new bank account.
signals.quote: We have moved our banking to a new provider. Please update your records so the payment for invoice FS-2026-1182 goes to our new account:

signals.explanation: Imposes a Friday deadline to pressure immediate action on the bank change.
signals.quote: Payments sent to the old account will be returned, so please make the change before Friday.

skeptic.argument: I cannot honestly argue benign here. The sender domain is not on file and closely resembles the known vendor's domain, indicating impersonation, while the email requests diversion of payment for invoice FS-2026-1182 to a new IBAN under time pressure and confirmation by reply. That combination fits a classic business-email-compromise fraud pattern with no benign explanation for both the domain mismatch and the bank-detail change.
skeptic.evidence_that_would_change_my_mind: Call Fennimore Stationery Ltd on a phone number already on file independent of this email and confirm directly that they sent this remittance notice and that GB03 ZZTB 6091 7233 0198 44 is their new account.
